node.title: Re: Store the outcome of a foreach loop in an array
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
The code you've showed appears to work fine for me - maybe $lines doesn't contain what you think it does? In [https://webperl.zero-g.net/democode/perleditor.html#%7B%22cmdline%22%3A%22perl%20script.pl%22%2C%22script%22%3A%22use%20warnings%3B%5Cnuse%20strict%3B%5Cnuse%20Data%3A%3ADumper%3B%5Cn%24Data%3A%3ADumper%3A%3AUseqq%3D1%3B%5Cn%5Cnmy%20%24lines%20%3D%20%5B%5C%22A%2CB%2CC%5C%22%2C%5C%22D%2CE%2CF%5C%22%2C%5C%22G%2CH%2CI%5C%22%5D%3B%5Cnprint%20Dumper(%24lines)%3B%5Cnmy%20%40store%3B%5Cnforeach%20my%20%24line%20(%40%24lines)%20%7B%5Cn%20%20%20%20my%20%40val%20%3D%20split(%2F%5C%5C%2C%2F%2C%24line)%3B%5Cn%5Ctprint%20Dumper(%5C%5C%40val)%3B%5Cn%20%20%20%20push%20(%40store%2C%40val%5B2%5D)%3B%5Cn%7D%5Cnprint%20Dumper(%5C%5C%40store)%3B%22%2C%22script_fn%22%3A%22script.pl%22%2C%22autorun%22%3Atrue%7D|this WebPerl live demo] (requires a modern browser), I've shown how to use [doc://Data::Dumper] to inspect data structures.

You should probably also heed the warning that Perl gives you: "Scalar value @val[2] better written as $val[2] "- the former is a [doc://perldata#Slices|"slice"] and is not the best way to access a single array element.

Update: Code from WebPerl reproduced here:

use warnings; use strict; use Data::Dumper; $Data::Dumper::Useqq=1; my $lines = ["A,B,C","D,E,F","G,H,I"]; print Dumper($lines); my @store; foreach my $line (@$lines) { my @val = split(/\,/,$line); print Dumper(\@val); push (@store,@val[2]); } print Dumper(\@store);
